newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, led by PGMs.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, led by PGMs.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Friday, as gold and silver continued to consolidate after seeing multi-year lows last month, while platinum group metals (PGMs) recovered further to set new contract highs.
"On gold and silver, I was bearish before and I'm still bearish," Smith Barney's Chicago based analyst Phil Tiger said. "I think gold is going to test the $300 level and silver the $4.00 level."

"The PGMs are the only metals that are truly in a shortage as the fact of the matter is there really isn't enough palladium to go around if everybody decided they wanted it today, and so platinum is entitled to have a $100 premium over gold."

COMEX December gold ended up 30 cents at $328.90 an ounce, but not before slipping to its lows for the week early at $327.30 an ounce. COMEX gold saw its lightest volume day this week though at 31,000 lots.

COMEX gold open interest continued to fall Thursday, dropping 3,677 lots to 184,713 contracts, its lowest level in a month, as funds continued to reduc the record net short positions built up in June.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $324.40/90, compared with the London Friday afternoon fix at $324.10 and the New York close Thursday at $324.30/80.

Gold as usual failed to respond to the latest U.S. economic news in which U.S. unemployment fell to 4.8 percent, its lowest level in 24 years, and June personal income rose 0.6 percent, and non-farm payrolls rose 316,000 in July.

But U.S. treasury bond yields fell sharply, dragging U.S. stockmarket prices down, after the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) data for July turned out to be much stronger than expected.
COMEX September silver ended down 2.0 cents at $4.447 an ounce, giving back some of Thursday's sharp gains, after a breakout from a three week old range between $4.20 and $4.40.

But NYMEX September palladium was locked limit up all day, closing up $6.00 at $206.60 an ounce, at a new contract high, with the December 1997 and March 1998 contracts also limit bid at new contract highs.
Palladium went limit up for the third day in a row on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) on Friday also, on heavy broker shortcovering, traders said.
Spot palladium ended quoted $224.60/227.60 an ounce, its highest levels since a 17 year high was seen in June around $240.00.
NYMEX October platinum gained $13.00 to end at $438.50 an ounce, after seeing a new contract high at $439.00.

The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread soared to new contract highs at $111.40 an ounce, and the platinum/gold spread in the spot market looked to be heading back towards levels last seen in the 1980's, analysts said.
Spot platinum ended quoted $440.00/443.00, its highest levels since June when a seven year high at $500.00 was seen.

No further Russian shipments of platinum group metals (PGMs) are expected in Japan under the annual supply contract until at least August 6, and offerings earlier this week by Russia in the spot market of parcels of only about 15,000 ounces of platinum are not meeting demand, traders said.

"The exact size of the shipment (to Japan) is not yet known, and Japan has almost completely run out of supplies of platinum," analyst Richard Harrison of brokers T. Hoare & Co said in a weekly report.
Russian exports of PGMs resumed in July after a six months suspension. Russia supplies about 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 percent of its palladium.

Meanwhile, South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats) said Friday all workers at its platinum refineries had reported for work desite the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) notice of a strike on Thursday.

The NUM said later Friday that the strike had been put on hold while the South African Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration considered the wage dispute. Implats produced 499,000 ounces of platinum in the second half of 1996.
South Africa supplies about 690 percent of the world's platinum and about 20 percent of its palladium.
